phrases.translation: All praise is for Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Complete praise and thanks belong to Allah alone, the owner of everything in the heavens and the earth. Nothing within them belongs independently to the beings people worship or to anyone else. His universal ownership makes Him uniquely worthy of praise, while every favor reaching their inhabitants comes from Him rather than from a partner sharing His dominion.

phrases.translation: And praise be to Him in the Hereafter.
phrases.explanation: Allah is equally worthy of complete praise in the Hereafter, just as in worldly life. His favors are not limited to the present world. They will continue in the life to come, so gratitude belongs purely to Him across both stages of existence. No other being shares in creating those favors or deserves a share of the praise for them.

phrases.translation: He is the All-Wise, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: Allah is wise in managing creation and guiding it according to His decree. He is fully aware of His servants, what benefits them, what they have done, and what they will do. His wisdom and knowledge encompass every detail, providing the foundation for the perfect ownership and generosity praised in the opening statements.

phrases.translation: He knows whatever goes into the earth and whatever comes out of it,
phrases.explanation: Allah knows everything that enters the earth and becomes hidden within it, as well as everything that emerges from it. Nothing concealed below its surface escapes Him, and nothing coming forth is outside His awareness. The paired movements emphasize complete knowledge of what people can see and what remains hidden from them.

phrases.translation: and whatever descends from the sky and whatever ascends into it.
phrases.explanation: He also knows whatever descends from the sky and whatever ascends into it. Together with the movements into and out of the earth, this covers all directions and realms of creation. The verse presents a knowledge without gaps, reaching every visible or concealed thing throughout the heavens and the earth.

phrases.translation: And He is the Most Merciful, All-Forgiving
phrases.explanation: Allah is merciful and forgiving toward servants who repent. He does not punish them after their accepted return, and He forgives the sins they abandon. These names follow the declaration of complete knowledge, showing that the One from whom nothing is hidden also provides a merciful path back for those who turn to Him.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say, “The Hour will never come to us.”
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers denied that Allah could restore creation after it perished and mockingly asked about the Hour. Their statement rejected the Prophet's warning rather than expressing a sincere request for knowledge. They assumed that death and dissolution placed them beyond restoration, so they treated the promised resurrection as an empty threat.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Yes—by my Lord, the Knower of the unseen—it will certainly come to you!”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet must answer with an oath by his Lord that the Hour will certainly reach them. Allah, who knows the unseen, affirms its arrival while reserving knowledge of its exact timing to Himself. The oath directly overturns their denial and leaves no room for the uncertainty they tried to spread.

phrases.translation: Not ˹even˺ an atom’s weight is hidden from Him in the heavens or the earth;
phrases.explanation: Not even an atom's weight anywhere in the heavens or the earth is hidden from Allah. What seems invisible or insignificant to created beings remains fully known to Him. This comprehensive knowledge supports the certainty of resurrection, since no part of creation can disappear beyond His awareness or escape His record.

phrases.translation: nor anything smaller or larger than that, but is ˹written˺ in a perfect Record
phrases.explanation: Nothing smaller or greater than an atom escapes Him either. Everything is recorded in a clear Book that demonstrates His complete enumeration and knowledge. The statement moves from the smallest imaginable measure to everything below and above it, closing every possible exception to the reach of divine knowledge.

phrases.translation: So He may reward those who believe and do good.
phrases.explanation: The clear record includes the recompense of those who believe in Allah and His Messenger and act righteously. Their good deeds mean following divine and prophetic commands while avoiding what Allah forbids. The promised reward answers their obedience, joining inward faith with conduct rather than separating belief from action.

phrases.translation: It is they who will have forgiveness and an honourable provision
phrases.explanation: Those believers receive forgiveness from their Lord for their sins and an honorable provision. The commentary explains that provision as a pleasant life in Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. The promise therefore includes both removal of past sin and generous future wellbeing, granted together to people of faithful obedience.

phrases.translation: As for those who strive to discredit Our revelations,
phrases.explanation: In contrast, some people work together to nullify Allah's revelations, proofs, and arguments. They strive against the signs while imagining that their own strength can make them escape Allah's power. Their opposition is active and organized, not simple misunderstanding, and their supposed ability to frustrate divine guidance is an illusion.

phrases.translation: it is they who will suffer the ˹worst˺ torment of agonizing pain
phrases.explanation: Those who strive against the revelations will receive an agonizing punishment described as an evil torment. Their efforts cannot make them escape Allah, despite their assumptions. The verse places their painful recompense beside the believers' forgiveness and honorable provision, showing the opposite outcomes of faithful obedience and deliberate resistance to divine proofs.

phrases.translation: Those gifted with knowledge ˹clearly˺ see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord ˹O Prophet˺ is the truth,
phrases.explanation: Those given knowledge recognize that the revelation sent to Muhammad from his Lord is the truth. Reports identify them as Muslims from the People of the Book who knew earlier scriptures, including Abdullah ibn Salam, or as the Prophet's companions. The interpretations differ over the knowledgeable group, but both affirm their informed recognition of the Quran's truth.

phrases.translation: and that it guides to the Path of the Almighty, the Praiseworthy
phrases.explanation: The revealed Book guides whoever follows and practices it to Islam and the path of Allah. He is almighty in recompensing His enemies and praiseworthy among creation because His blessings and favors are abundant. Guidance therefore leads toward the One whose power establishes justice and whose generosity makes Him worthy of continual praise.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers say ˹mockingly to one another˺, “Shall we show you a man who claims that when you have been utterly disintegrated you will be raised as a new creation
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers mockingly pointed others toward Muhammad because he taught that people would be created anew after complete disintegration. They imagined bodies decaying into dust and bones or being torn by animals and birds, then found restoration incredible. Their question ridiculed the message of resurrection by presenting the Prophet's promise as something astonishing and unbelievable.

phrases.translation: Has he fabricated a lie against Allah or is he insane?”
phrases.explanation: In their denial of resurrection, the disbelievers suggested that Muhammad had either invented a lie against Allah or was insane and speaking without understanding. These were accusations intended to discredit the source of the promise, not genuine alternatives established by evidence. Their mockery of renewed creation developed into an attack on the Messenger himself.

phrases.translation: In fact, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are bound for torment and have strayed farthest ˹from the truth˺
phrases.explanation: Allah rejects those accusations and turns the judgment back on people who deny the Hereafter. They face His punishment and are far astray from truth and the straight path. Their distance from guidance explains their slander against the Prophet. The real deception lies in their denial, not in his divinely confirmed message of resurrection.

phrases.translation: Have they not then seen all that surrounds them of the heavens and the earth?
phrases.explanation: The deniers are asked to consider the heavens and earth before them, behind them, and on every side. Wherever they go, they remain surrounded by Allah's creation and within His reach. Reflection on this setting should have restrained their ignorance and denial, since no direction offers independence from His power.

phrases.translation: If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them up, or cause ˹deadly˺ pieces of the sky to fall upon them.
phrases.explanation: If Allah willed, He could make the earth swallow these deniers or send down deadly fragments of the sky upon them. The One who surrounds them through creation can also command that creation against them. Their security is therefore never self-created, and their rejection cannot place them beyond immediate divine power.

phrases.translation: Surely in this is a sign for every servant who turns ˹to Allah˺
phrases.explanation: The surrounding heavens and earth contain a sign for every servant who returns to Allah in repentance. Such a servant recognizes His oneness, sovereignty, uniqueness, and right to obedience. The sign demonstrates that nothing prevents Allah from accomplishing what He wills, making both resurrection and the warned punishment entirely within His capability.

phrases.translation: Indeed, We granted David a ˹great˺ privilege from Us, ˹commanding:˺
phrases.explanation: Allah granted David a special privilege from His own bounty. The favors that follow were divine gifts rather than achievements David could claim through unaided ability. Introducing them as grace sets the pattern for understanding the extraordinary control over worshipping creation and materials described next.

phrases.translation: “O mountains! Echo his hymns! And the birds as well.”
phrases.explanation: Allah commanded the mountains to glorify with David when he glorified, and the birds joined in the same response. The language of echoing means returning praise together with him. His hymns were therefore accompanied by creation itself, marking a remarkable favor in which his worship resonated through both mountains and birds.

phrases.translation: We made iron mouldable for him
phrases.explanation: Allah made iron soft for David so that he could shape it directly with his hand. Reports compare it to moist clay and state that he did not need fire or an iron tool to beat it into form. This miraculous pliability was another expression of the privilege granted to him.

phrases.translation: instructing: “Make full-length armour,
phrases.explanation: Allah instructed David to make complete coats of mail. Reports describe him as the first to make this linked armour, which had previously consisted of plates. The pliable iron granted in the preceding verse was therefore used for a particular craft taught and commanded by Allah.

phrases.translation: ˹perfectly˺ balancing the links.
phrases.explanation: He had to measure the armour's rings and rivets carefully. A rivet too thick could break its ring, while one made too thin or small could come loose and rattle. The command required precise proportion and skilled construction, not merely shaping metal arbitrarily after it became soft.

phrases.translation: And work righteousness ˹O family of David!˺.
phrases.explanation: David and his family were commanded to act righteously through obedience to Allah. Extraordinary material skill did not replace moral responsibility. Their work and lives were to express righteousness, showing that the purpose of divine favors extends beyond technical achievement to faithful conduct in every circumstance.

phrases.translation: Indeed, I am All-Seeing of what you do.”
phrases.explanation: Allah sees everything David, his family, and their followers do. Nothing of their work remains hidden from Him, and He will requite them for all of it. This closing statement makes both craftsmanship and righteous action accountable before the One whose vision is complete and perfect.

phrases.translation: And to Solomon ˹We subjected˺ the wind: its morning stride was a month’s journey and so was its evening stride.
phrases.explanation: Allah subjected the wind to Solomon. Its morning journey covered the distance normally traveled in a month, and its evening journey covered another month's distance. The commentary summarizes this as traveling two months' journey in a single day, demonstrating extraordinary speed granted through divine control of the wind.

phrases.translation: And We caused a stream of molten copper to flow for him,
phrases.explanation: Allah melted a source of copper and made it flow for Solomon. Reports compare its movement to flowing water and describe the metal as workable like dough. This favor parallels the softening of iron for David while remaining a distinct miracle concerning copper for Solomon.

phrases.translation: and ˹We subjected˺ some of the jinn to work under him by his Lord’s Will.
phrases.explanation: Some jinn worked under Solomon, obeying his commands and avoiding what he prohibited. Their service occurred only by Allah's permission, command, and act of subjecting them to him. Solomon's authority over them was therefore delegated, not an independent power that he possessed apart from his Lord.

phrases.translation: And whoever of them deviated from Our command, We made them taste the torment of the blaze
phrases.explanation: Any jinn who deviated from Allah's command to obey Solomon would taste the punishment of the blazing Fire in the Hereafter. The warning makes clear that their required service was itself a divine command. Resisting Solomon in that assigned duty meant departing from Allah's order and incurring His punishment.

phrases.translation: They made for him whatever he desired of sanctuaries, statues,
phrases.explanation: The jinn made whatever Solomon desired, including sanctuaries and other structures used as dwellings, palaces, mosques, or places of worship. They also made statues, described in reports as works of copper and glass. These products display the range of skilled labor included in their divinely permitted service.

phrases.translation: basins as large as reservoirs, and cooking pots fixed ˹into the ground˺.
phrases.explanation: They fashioned basins as large as pools or reservoirs where water could collect, along with enormous cooking pots that remained fixed in place. The pots were too large to move or transport. Their immense scale further illustrates the unusual constructions and utensils produced for Solomon.

phrases.translation: ˹We ordered:˺ “Work gratefully, O family of David!”
phrases.explanation: David's family were told to work in gratitude for the special favors Allah had given them and for the blessings shared with other creatures. Gratitude here means obeying Allah, fearing Him, and doing what pleases Him for His sake. Praise forms part of that gratitude, but obedient action gives it practical expression.

phrases.translation: ˹Only˺ a few of My servants are ˹truly˺ grateful
phrases.explanation: Only a few of Allah's servants are truly grateful. The commentary describes them as people sincere in affirming His oneness and devoted exclusively to obeying Him and thanking Him for His blessings. Genuine gratitude is therefore uncommon and comprehensive, joining worship, loyalty, and thankful recognition rather than words alone.

phrases.translation: When We decreed Solomon’s death, nothing indicated to the ˹subjected˺ jinn that he was dead except the termites eating away his staff.
phrases.explanation: When Allah caused Solomon to die, nothing revealed his death to the jinn except a wood-eating creature gnawing at the staff on which he leaned. The creature gradually weakened the staff until it could no longer support him. An ordinary insect, rather than their supposed knowledge, exposed what had happened.

phrases.translation: So when he collapsed,
phrases.explanation: Solomon fell when the damaged staff gave way, making his death visible. His collapse was the outward event that ended the jinn's false assumption that he remained alive. Reports describe him as having remained supported in prayer while they continued working, unaware of his condition.

phrases.translation: the jinn realized that if they had ˹really˺ known the unseen, they would not have remained in ˹such˺ humiliating servitude
phrases.explanation: The jinn's ignorance of the unseen became clear when he fell. Reports say they had continued their humiliating labor for a full year, thinking Solomon was alive. Had they truly known the unseen, they would not have remained in that servitude. The event exposed their claims before humanity and confirmed that such knowledge was not theirs.

phrases.translation: Indeed, there was a sign for ˹the tribe of˺ Sheba in their homeland: two orchards—one to the right and the other to the left.
phrases.explanation: The descendants of Sheba had a clear sign of their Lord's favor in their homeland: two lush orchards situated on the right and left, described as lying between two mountains. Their remarkable productivity demonstrated that provision came from the One who blessed them, not from an independent power or another lord.

phrases.translation: ˹They were told:˺ “Eat from the provision of your Lord, and be grateful to Him.
phrases.explanation: They were invited to eat the crops and fruits Allah provided through those orchards and to thank Him for His favor. Enjoying the provision was joined directly with gratitude. The command did not require rejecting worldly blessing, but recognizing its source and responding with thankful obedience.

phrases.translation: ˹Yours is˺ a good land and a forgiving Lord.”
phrases.explanation: Their land was wholesome and abundant, with reports describing freedom from harmful pests and exceptional fertility. Alongside this earthly goodness stood their forgiving Lord, who would pardon their sins if they obeyed Him. Material blessing and the opportunity for divine forgiveness were both reasons for continued gratitude.

phrases.translation: But they turned away.
phrases.explanation: Sheba turned away from obeying its Lord and from following the messengers who called the people to their Creator. Their response to abundant provision was rejection rather than gratitude. Reports describe repeated prophetic warnings before the punishment, making the turning away a deliberate refusal of guidance.

phrases.translation: So We sent against them a devastating flood,
phrases.explanation: Allah sent the flood associated with their dam, which had held back and regulated the water. Reports describe a burrowing animal weakening the structure before the flood destroyed their land and gardens. The commentary favors this account of water overwhelming them over an interpretation that it was merely diverted away.

phrases.translation: and replaced their orchards with two others producing bitter fruit, fruitless bushes, and a few ˹sparse˺ thorny trees
phrases.explanation: Their fruitful orchards were replaced with growth producing bitter fruit, fruitless bushes such as tamarisk, and only a few thorny trees. What had been among the best vegetation became among the worst because of their deeds. The loss transformed both the taste and usefulness of their land's produce.

phrases.translation: This is how We rewarded them for their ingratitude.
phrases.explanation: The destruction of Sheba's possessions and gardens was recompense for their ingratitude, disbelief in Allah, and rejection of His messengers. The flood was therefore not detached from their moral response to blessing. It answered a sustained pattern of denying the One who had provided for them and refusing the guidance sent to them.

phrases.translation: Would We ever punish ˹anyone in such a way˺ except the ungrateful
phrases.explanation: The requital singled out here is punishment according to exact desert for the profoundly ungrateful. It does not deny Allah's reward to believers. The commentary contrasts His bounty toward faith, which multiplies good deeds, with repayment for grave sin and disbelief without the same gracious multiplication or erasure.

phrases.translation: We had also placed between them and the cities We showered with blessings ˹many small˺ towns within sight of one another.
phrases.explanation: Allah placed visible, closely connected towns between Sheba and the blessed cities. Reports identify the destination region as Syria or the Holy Land, including Jerusalem. These intermediate settlements made the route populated and accessible rather than leaving travelers isolated across an empty and dangerous expanse.

phrases.translation: And We set moderate travel distances in between,
phrases.explanation: The stages of travel were measured from one town and stopping place to another. Travelers could lodge in a settlement and depart from another without facing excessive distances between them. This thoughtful arrangement was another divine favor, making ordinary movement manageable and well supplied on their route.

phrases.translation: ˹saying,˺ “Travel between them by day and night safely.”
phrases.explanation: They could travel through these settlements by day or night in safety, without fearing hunger, thirst, or injustice. Reports describe journeys without carrying provisions or water because resources were readily available. Safety therefore included both personal security and freedom from basic deprivation throughout the route.

phrases.translation: But they said, “Our Lord! Make ˹the distances of˺ our journeys longer,” wronging themselves.
phrases.explanation: Instead of valuing easy and safe travel, they asked Allah to lengthen their journeys, desiring deserts where they would need mounts and provisions. This request showed insolence toward His favor and ignorance of the value of wellbeing. By choosing what angered Allah through disobedience, they wronged themselves and invited punishment.

phrases.translation: So We reduced them to ˹cautionary˺ tales,
phrases.explanation: Allah made their story a lesson repeated among people. Their dispersion became proverbial as an example of a community breaking apart after turning against blessing. They were no longer known simply for prosperous gardens and secure travel, but for a downfall that others could recount and heed.

phrases.translation: and scattered them utterly.
phrases.explanation: Allah scattered the people throughout different lands in a complete dispersal. Reports associate various descendant groups with Syria, Medina, Tihamah, Oman, and other regions. Their former unity in a favored homeland was broken, fulfilling the loss of ease and cohesion that their ungrateful request had helped bring upon them.

phrases.translation: Surely in this are lessons for whoever is steadfast, grateful
phrases.explanation: Their account contains lessons for every deeply patient and grateful servant. Gratitude is required when Allah bestows favors, and patience is required when He tests someone with adversity. Sheba's example teaches both responses by showing the danger of resentful abundance and the value of steadfast thankfulness in every condition.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Iblîs’ assumption about them has come true,
phrases.explanation: Iblis had assumed that most people would not be grateful and had threatened to lead them astray. The commentary stresses that this was an assumption, not certain knowledge of the unseen. Events confirmed his expectation when many followed his misguidance, just as the earlier account exposed ingratitude despite abundant blessings.

phrases.translation: so they ˹all˺ follow him, except a group of ˹true˺ believers
phrases.explanation: They followed Iblis into disobedience, except for a group of true believers. Those believers remained firm in obeying Allah and disobeying Iblis. Their exception prevents the verse from making his success absolute and shows that steadfast faith can resist the pattern of ingratitude and misguidance found among the rest.

phrases.translation: He does not have any authority over them,
phrases.explanation: Iblis had no compelling power or independent authority over the people he misled. He did not force them with a weapon, but invited them through desires and deception within the trial Allah permitted. Their following was therefore not proof that he possessed controlling lordship over them.

phrases.translation: but ˹Our Will is˺ only to distinguish those who believe in the Hereafter from those who are in doubt about it.
phrases.explanation: The permitted trial makes visibly distinct those who believe in resurrection, reward, and punishment from those who remain uncertain about the Hereafter. This distinction becomes evident through response and conduct, forming a basis for deserved recompense. It is not a claim that Allah previously lacked knowledge of people.

phrases.translation: And your Lord is a ˹vigilant˺ Keeper over all things.”
phrases.explanation: The Lord keeps watch over every deed and everything else. Nothing escapes His knowledge, and He will requite all people on the Day of Resurrection for the good and evil they acquired in worldly life. His complete preservation of the record secures the outcome of the distinction just described.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Call upon those you claim ˹to be divine˺ besides Allah.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet must challenge the polytheists to call upon the beings they claim as divine partners. They should ask those beings to produce blessing or loss like the acts of Allah already recounted. Their inability would expose the error of attributing lordship to anything besides Allah.

phrases.translation: They do not possess ˹even˺ an atom’s weight either in the heavens or the earth,
phrases.explanation: These supposed deities do not own even an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth. They control no independent portion through which they could cause benefit or harm. Beings with no ownership at all cannot rightly be treated as gods or sources of provision.

phrases.translation: nor do they have any share in ˹governing˺ them.
phrases.explanation: They possess no share in the heavens or earth, whether through divided ownership or a common undivided share. The statement closes both possible ways of claiming a property interest. They neither own anything independently nor participate with Allah in owning any part of creation whatsoever.

phrases.translation: Nor is any of them a helper to Him.”
phrases.explanation: None of these supposed partners assists Allah in creating or preserving the heavens and earth. A claim of partnership cannot be based on help rendered, because no such help exists. With no ownership, no share, and no assisting role, nothing remains on which to justify worshipping them alongside Him.

phrases.translation: No intercession will be of any benefit with Him, except by those granted permission by Him.
phrases.explanation: No intercessor can benefit anyone with Allah except where He grants permission for that intercession. The commentary explains that no such permission is given on behalf of disbelievers. Worshipping idols in hopes of gaining nearness or intercession is therefore baseless, since the entire matter depends on Allah's authorization.

phrases.translation: ˹At last,˺ when the dread ˹of Judgment Day˺ is relieved from their hearts ˹because they are permitted to intercede˺, they will ˹excitedly˺ ask ˹the angels˺, “What has your Lord ˹just˺ said?”
phrases.explanation: The preferred reports describe angels overwhelmed by fear when Allah's revelation or command is heard, then asking one another what the Lord said after that fear is lifted. The scene concerns their awe and subsequent reassurance, not independent angelic doubt about the content of divine speech.

phrases.translation: The angels will reply, “The truth!
phrases.explanation: The angels answer that Allah spoke the truth. His speech contains no falsehood, and He fulfills what He promises. Their response affirms complete confidence in what was revealed, answering the question with the essential character of divine speech rather than with speculation or contradictory reports.

phrases.translation: And He is the Most High, All-Great.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is exalted above all things and supreme in greatness. These attributes close the scene by directing attention from the angels' awe to the majesty of the One who spoke. His exaltation and greatness befit the reverent response described and the unquestionable truth of His word.

phrases.translation: Ask ˹them, O Prophet˺, “Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?”
phrases.explanation: The question identifies Allah's provision through rain that sustains crops, the sun, moon, and stars that serve human benefit, and food brought from the earth for people and livestock. Provision from above and below encompasses the systems on which life depends. The audience is asked to recognize the source of these everyday blessings.

phrases.translation: Say, “Allah!
phrases.explanation: If the audience cannot answer, the Prophet must state plainly that Allah is the provider of all these things. The One supplying rain, food, and the beneficial order of creation is not one of their idols. Their dependence on His provision undermines their attempt to assign His lordship to powerless partners.

phrases.translation: Now, certainly one of our two groups is ˹rightly˺ guided; the other is clearly astray.”
phrases.explanation: One of the two groups is guided and the other clearly astray, since both cannot hold the same truth. This wording does not express real uncertainty in the Prophet. The commentary explains it as a restrained way of charging the opponents with error, while reports explicitly identify the believers as guided and the polytheists as astray.

phrases.translation: Say, “You will not be accountable for our misdeeds, nor will we be accountable for your deeds.”
phrases.explanation: Each group answers for its own conduct. The polytheists will not be questioned for wrongdoing committed by the believers, and the believers will not be questioned for the deeds of the polytheists. This establishes individual responsibility and prepares for the final judgment, where Allah will reveal which side followed guidance and which followed error.

phrases.translation: Say, “Our Lord will gather us together, then He will judge between us with the truth.
phrases.explanation: The Lord will gather believers and their opponents together on the Day of Resurrection and judge between them with truth and justice. That judgment will make clear which group followed guidance and which followed error. The disputes of worldly life therefore end before a decisive divine adjudication, not through mere victory in argument.

phrases.translation: For He is the All-Knowing Judge.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is the judge who knows everything. Nothing hidden remains concealed from Him, and He needs no witnesses to distinguish the just from the unjust. His judgment is therefore both truthful and fully informed, unlike a human decision based on incomplete evidence or outward appearances.

phrases.translation: Say, “Show me those ˹idols˺ you have joined with Him as partners.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet must ask the polytheists to display the idols and images they attached to Allah as partners in worship. The challenge calls for evidence of their divine status, such as what they created on earth or what share they possess in the heavens. Their supposed partnership cannot survive this demand for proof.

phrases.translation: No! In fact, He ˹alone˺ is Allah—
phrases.explanation: Their claim is rejected completely. Allah alone is the true object of worship, without any partner in His dominion. Partnership does not befit Him, and the polytheists' description is false. Divine unity is affirmed not merely as a preference but as the reality that excludes every alleged associate.

phrases.translation: the Almighty, All-Wise.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is almighty in taking retribution against those who associate partners with Him and wise in governing His creatures. His power secures justice against false worship, while His wisdom orders all affairs. These attributes answer the challenged claim by presenting the sole God as both sovereign in rule and perfect in judgment.

phrases.translation: We have sent you ˹O Prophet˺ only as a deliverer of good news and a warner to all of humanity,
phrases.explanation: Muhammad was sent not only to the polytheists of his own people but to all humanity, Arabs and non-Arabs alike. He brings good news to those who obey him and warns those who deny him. The commentary adds that honor with Allah depends on obedience rather than ethnic identity.

phrases.translation: but most people do not know
phrases.explanation: Most people do not know that Allah sent Muhammad with this universal mission. Their lack of knowledge does not narrow the scope of his sending. The statement distinguishes the actual breadth of the prophetic message from widespread human unawareness of its purpose and worldwide reach.

phrases.translation: And they ask ˹the believers˺, “When will this threat come to pass, if what you say is true?”
phrases.explanation: When the polytheists hear Allah's warning about what will happen to disbelievers after their return to Him, they demand its date and question the believers' truthfulness. Their question treats the threatened resurrection and recompense as doubtful. It repeats the earlier pattern of challenging divine warnings rather than responding to their moral demand.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “A Day has ˹already˺ been appointed for you, which you can neither delay nor advance by a ˹single˺ moment.”
phrases.explanation: The threatened Day already has a fixed appointment. When it arrives, they cannot postpone it even briefly to gain further time for repentance, nor can they bring its punishment forward before the term Allah set. Human demands neither control nor alter its timing, which remains entirely under divine determination.

phrases.translation: The disbelievers vow, “We will never believe in this Quran, nor in those ˹Scriptures˺ before it.”
phrases.explanation: The Arab polytheists vowed never to believe in the Quran brought by Muhammad or in the earlier scriptures and prophets. Their rejection extended beyond one messenger to the wider chain of revelation. This settled refusal set the stage for the later confrontation in which its participants blame one another.

phrases.translation: If only you could see when the wrongdoers will be detained before their Lord, throwing blame at each other!
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers will be detained before their Lord, reproaching and disputing with one another. Their former unity in rejecting revelation breaks down under judgment before Him. The scene exposes conflict between followers and leaders who had shared disbelief but now seek to place responsibility elsewhere.

phrases.translation: The lowly ˹followers˺ will say to the arrogant ˹leaders˺, “Had it not been for you, we would certainly have been believers.”
phrases.explanation: Those who had been lowly and dominated in worldly life will tell their arrogant leaders that they would have believed in Allah and His signs if not for them. The accusation identifies the leaders' influence over their followers. It begins an exchange about responsibility rather than ending it with one side's claim.

phrases.translation: The arrogant will respond to the lowly, “Did we ever hinder you from guidance after it came to you?
phrases.explanation: The arrogant leaders will ask whether they actually turned their followers away from guidance after it had already reached them and become clear. Their reply attempts to deny responsibility for obstructing a message that was available to the followers. The dispute thus concerns the significance of having received guidance before choosing disbelief.

phrases.translation: In fact, you were wicked ˹on your own˺.”
phrases.explanation: The leaders tell the lowly that they were themselves wicked. Their own preference for disbelief over faith prevented them from following guidance and believing in Allah and His Messenger. This answer challenges the attempt to place all blame on others, emphasizing the followers' own corrupt choice alongside the leaders' misguidance.

phrases.translation: The lowly will say to the arrogant, “No! It was your plotting by day and night—when you ordered us to disbelieve in Allah and to set up equals with Him.”
phrases.explanation: The lowly answer that their leaders plotted against them continuously by day and night. Those leaders commanded them to disbelieve in Allah and to establish equals and partners with Him in worship and divinity. The followers thus identify deliberate, ongoing misguidance rather than an isolated mistake by their leaders.

phrases.translation: They will ˹all˺ hide ˹their˺ remorse when they see the torment.
phrases.explanation: When they see Allah's punishment, they will feel and conceal remorse among themselves over having neglected obedience to Him in worldly life. Their regret comes only when its consequences stand before them. It does not undo the choices whose neglect and wrongdoing are now being recompensed.

phrases.translation: And We will put shackles around the necks of the disbelievers.
phrases.explanation: Allah will place shackles around the disbelievers' necks, with reports describing their hands fastened to their necks in the Fire. This restraint forms part of their recompense for disbelieving during worldly life. The image makes their helplessness under judgment unmistakable after their former arrogance and mutual accusations.

phrases.translation: Will they be rewarded except for what they used to do
phrases.explanation: They are recompensed only for the corrupt deeds they used to perform. The punishment is therefore presented as a just response to their own conduct, not as an arbitrary injury. Both misleading leadership and willing participation in disbelief fall within the deeds for which they are held accountable.

phrases.translation: Whenever We sent a warner to a society, its elite would say, “We truly reject what you have been sent with.”
phrases.explanation: Whenever Allah sent a warner to a town, its affluent chiefs and leaders in misguidance rejected the message. They denied the warning of divine punishment and the call to affirm Allah's oneness and abandon idols and partners. The verse presents a recurring pattern across communities, not an objection unique to Muhammad's immediate audience.

phrases.translation: Adding, “We are far superior ˹to the believers˺ in wealth and children, and we will never be punished.”
phrases.explanation: These arrogant elites boasted of greater wealth and children and assumed they would never be punished in the Hereafter. They interpreted material abundance as evidence that Allah approved of their beliefs and deeds and had drawn them near to Himself. Worldly privilege thus became their false argument for spiritual excellence and future immunity.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely ˹it is˺ my Lord ˹Who˺ gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills.
phrases.explanation: Allah expands or restricts worldly provision for whoever He wills among His creatures. Abundance does not necessarily show love, merit, or special nearness, and restriction does not necessarily show hatred. He distributes both as a trial and test for His servants rather than as simple public evidence of their spiritual rank.

phrases.translation: But most people do not know.”
phrases.explanation: Most people do not understand this purpose. They assume that expanded provision proves divine love and restricted provision proves divine hatred. That mistake explains the elite's confidence in their wealth and children. The verse corrects the assumption by placing material circumstances within a test whose significance cannot be read so simply.

phrases.translation: It is not your wealth or children that bring you closer to Us.
phrases.explanation: Wealth and children, in which people boast, do not themselves bring anyone nearer to Allah. People are not judged by how much of either they possess. A disbeliever may receive abundant wealth while a believer experiences restriction, so material quantity cannot serve as the measure of acceptance or closeness.

phrases.translation: But those who believe and do good—it is they who will have a multiplied reward for what they did,
phrases.explanation: Faith and righteous action are what truly matter. One reported explanation adds that believers' wealth and children can contribute to nearness when used in obedience and fulfillment of Allah's rights. The promised reward is multiplied, with reports describing at least tenfold for good deeds and still greater multiplication for spending in Allah's way.

phrases.translation: and they will be secure in ˹elevated˺ mansions
phrases.explanation: People of faith and righteous deeds will be secure in the elevated chambers of Paradise, safe from Allah's punishment. Their lasting honor contrasts with the elite's reliance on temporary wealth and descendants. Security in those gardens, rather than worldly abundance, is the true sign of a favored outcome.

phrases.translation: As for those who strive to discredit Our revelations, it is they who will be confined in punishment
phrases.explanation: Those who work together against Allah's revelations seek to nullify His proofs and extinguish the light of His Book. They imagine that their efforts can make them escape Him or render Him powerless. Instead, they will be brought to the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection, unable to avoid the judgment they opposed.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “Surely ˹it is˺ my Lord ˹Who˺ gives abundant or limited provisions to whoever He wills of His servants.
phrases.explanation: Allah expands provision for whichever servants He wills and restricts it for others. Either condition may occur with or without honor or humiliation, since its purpose includes trial and testing. The verse repeats the principle that material allowance alone cannot reveal a servant's standing with Allah.

phrases.translation: And whatever you spend in charity, He will compensate ˹you˺ for it.
phrases.explanation: Whatever people spend in obedience to Allah, He will replace and compensate. One report describes acceptable spending as neither wasted through excess nor made excessively little. The promise answers fear that charitable expenditure means unrewarded loss, placing what is given for Allah under His reliable recompense.

phrases.translation: For He is the Best Provider.”
phrases.explanation: Allah is the best of all providers. Others may be described as providing for a family or household, but their provision is limited and dependent. He surpasses everyone to whom that description is applied, making Him the sure source behind both daily sustenance and the replacement promised for obedient spending.

phrases.translation: And ˹consider˺ the Day He will gather them all together, and then ask the angels, “Was it you that these ˹polytheists˺ used to worship?”
phrases.explanation: On the Day when Allah gathers all the disbelievers, He will ask the angels whether these people used to worship them instead of Him. The question publicly confronts the object of their devotion. The angels then disassociate themselves from the worshippers, showing that the alleged partnership offered no support at judgment.

phrases.translation: They will say, “Glory be to You! Our loyalty is to You, not them.
phrases.explanation: The angels will glorify Allah and declare themselves free of the partners and equals attributed to Him. Their loyalty and protection belong to Him alone, not to their worshippers, and they take no protector besides Him. This directly renounces the devotion that people had misdirected toward them.

phrases.translation: In fact, they ˹only˺ followed the ˹temptations of evil˺ jinn,
phrases.explanation: The angels explain that these people were actually following and worshipping jinn rather than the angels. The objects of devotion named in worldly claims are thus distinguished from the influence that truly captured their obedience. Angelic worship cannot be used to legitimize what the angels themselves reject.

phrases.translation: in whom most of them had faith.”
phrases.explanation: Most of the worshippers believed the jinn and accepted their claims. The commentary includes the assertion that angels were Allah's daughters, a claim from which Allah is completely exalted. Their faith was placed in deceptive created beings rather than in the truth about Allah and His messengers.

phrases.translation: So Today neither of you can benefit or protect each other.
phrases.explanation: On that Day, neither the angels nor their former worshippers can benefit or harm one another. The angels cannot rescue those who devoted themselves to them, and no reciprocal power exists between the two sides. Every imagined advantage from that misplaced loyalty disappears at judgment.

phrases.translation: And We will say to the wrongdoers, “Taste the torment of the Fire, which you used to deny.”
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers placed worship in the wrong place by directing it to beings other than Allah, who alone deserves it. Allah will tell them to taste the Fire they used to deny in worldly life. What they once dismissed as unreal has now become their experienced recompense.

phrases.translation: When Our clear revelations are recited to them, they say, “This is only a man who wishes to hinder you from what your forefathers used to worship.”
phrases.explanation: When Allah's clear verses, demonstrating that they are truth from Him, are recited, the polytheists call Muhammad merely a man trying to turn them from ancestral idols. They defend inherited worship by portraying his call to change it as unacceptable interference rather than engaging with the clarity of the revelation.

phrases.translation: They also say, “This ˹Quran˺ is no more than a fabricated lie.”
phrases.explanation: They also dismiss the Quran recited to them as an invented and concocted falsehood. This accusation targets its divine origin, allowing them to avoid submitting to its message. Calling it fabricated does not answer its clear signs but supplies another reason for continuing their rejection.

phrases.translation: And the disbelievers say of the truth when it has come to them, “This is nothing but pure magic.”
phrases.explanation: When the truth comes to the disbelievers through Muhammad's prophetic mission, they label it obvious magic. The commentary applies this charge to the Prophet and the truth he brought. Their shifting descriptions of man, fabrication, and sorcery are repeated attempts to discredit revelation rather than responses grounded in proof.

phrases.translation: ˹They say so even though˺ We had never given them any scriptures to study,
phrases.explanation: These polytheists had not been given scriptures that they studied or read. They therefore had no inherited book supporting their accusations against Muhammad and his message. The statement exposes their confident labels as claims made without the scriptural foundation they might have claimed to possess.

phrases.translation: nor did We ever send them a warner before you ˹O Prophet˺
phrases.explanation: No warner had been sent to this particular people before Muhammad. The commentary applies this to the Arabs, stating that they had received no earlier prophet or scripture before him and the Quran. Their immediate opposition was therefore not a continuation of rejecting a prior messenger sent directly to them.

phrases.translation: Those ˹destroyed˺ before them denied as well—
phrases.explanation: Earlier communities likewise denied Allah's messengers and the revelation they brought. Muhammad's people were not the first to respond with rejection. This connection places their conduct within a history of communities whose response to divine warning carried serious consequences. Their rejection also brought divine punishment.

phrases.translation: and these ˹Meccans˺ have not attained even one-tenth of what We had given their predecessors.
phrases.explanation: The Meccans had not reached even a tenth of what earlier peoples received in strength, power, and other worldly favors. Their relative weakness made boasting about security especially misplaced. Greater resources had not protected previous deniers, so lesser resources could not establish immunity for these opponents.

phrases.translation: Yet ˹when˺ they denied My messengers, how severe was My response
phrases.explanation: When those earlier peoples denied the messengers, Allah punished them by changing and removing the favors He had given them. The Prophet is invited to consider how severe that response was. Their fate demonstrates that abundance never prevents divine recompense when revelation is openly rejected.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I advise you to do ˹only˺ one thing:
phrases.explanation: The Prophet offers one essential piece of advice: obey Allah. This single duty is explained as standing before Allah with sincere counsel and abandoning personal caprice. The instruction narrows their attention from numerous accusations and inherited loyalties to a constructive response they can sincerely undertake, rather than allowing hostility or desire to decide the matter.

phrases.translation: stand up for ˹the sake of˺ Allah—individually or in pairs—
phrases.explanation: They should stand before Allah alone or two at a time with sincerity and freedom from caprice. In pairs, they can honestly ask one another whether they have ever known madness in Muhammad. Alone, each can withdraw from crowd pressure and consider the question carefully.

phrases.translation: then reflect. Your fellow man is not insane.
phrases.explanation: After this reflection, they should recognize that their companion Muhammad is not insane. Sincere consultation and private thought are meant to replace reflexive accusations with an assessment of what they actually know about him. The verse appeals to their own direct knowledge rather than inherited hostility.

phrases.translation: He is only a warner to you before ˹the coming of˺ a severe punishment.”
phrases.explanation: Muhammad is only a warner to them before a severe punishment. He warns them about Hell because of their disbelief before they reach it, while warning can still benefit them. His role is therefore sincere counsel for their safety, not the irrational behavior alleged by his opponents.

phrases.translation: Say, “If I had ever asked you for a reward, you could keep it.
phrases.explanation: The Prophet asks for no payment in return for warning them about Allah's punishment or sincerely calling them to faith and obedience. If any reward had been requested, they could keep it. This removes the suspicion that his invitation is motivated by money he hopes to take from them.

phrases.translation: My reward is only from Allah.
phrases.explanation: His recompense for calling them to believe, obey Allah, and accept the delivered message rests with Allah alone. He does not depend on their fees or gifts. The source of his reward confirms that his mission is undertaken for his Lord rather than as a commercial service to his audience.

phrases.translation: And He is a Witness over all things.”
phrases.explanation: Allah witnesses the truth of what the Prophet says and bears witness to everything else as well. His testimony supports the sincerity of the Messenger's claim. No statement, motive, or action lies outside His observation, so He knows whether the call is truthful and whether its delivery is faithful.

phrases.translation: Say, “Surely my Lord hurls the truth ˹against falsehood˺.
phrases.explanation: Allah hurls the truth by sending revelation down from heaven to Muhammad, His chosen prophet and messenger. The image presents revelation as a powerful divine intervention against falsehood. Another explanation in the commentary describes Allah shattering falsehood with truth so that falsehood perishes and truth endures.

phrases.translation: ˹He is˺ the Knower of all unseen.”
phrases.explanation: Allah knows all unseen things, including what is hidden from sight and what has not yet come into existence but will be. This knowledge belongs uniquely to His lordship. The One who sends revelation therefore knows every hidden reality relevant to its truth and every future event it announces.

phrases.translation: Say, “The truth has come,
phrases.explanation: The truth that has clearly come is the Quran and Allah's revelation. Its arrival is a completed reality, not a proposed invention of the Prophet. The declaration follows the image of Allah hurling truth and announces the presence of guidance that falsehood cannot legitimately displace.

phrases.translation: and falsehood will vanish, never to return.”
phrases.explanation: Falsehood cannot bring creation into existence or restore it after perishing. The commentary identifies falsehood here with Iblis, who creates no one and resurrects no one. It also explains that falsehood then perishes when struck by truth, while divine truth alone remains established and enduring.

phrases.translation: Say, “If I am astray, the loss is only mine.
phrases.explanation: If the Prophet were to stray from right guidance, the harm of that straying would fall upon himself. The statement places responsibility for error on the one who commits it. It does not concede that he is astray, but clarifies the consequence within the hypothetical challenge to his opponents.

phrases.translation: And if I am guided, it is ˹only˺ because of what my Lord reveals to me.
phrases.explanation: If he is guided and remains firm upon truth, that guidance comes through Allah's revelation and the mercy that enables him to remain steadfast throughout his entire mission. He does not claim independent possession of guidance. Its source and sustaining power belong to his Lord.

phrases.translation: He is indeed All-Hearing, Ever Near.”
phrases.explanation: Allah hears what the Prophet and his audience say and preserves every word. He is near to every speaker, closer than the jugular vein, so no speech is distant or difficult for Him to hear. He will recompense the Prophet for his truthfulness and knows the responses of all others.

phrases.translation: If only you could see when they will be horrified with no escape ˹on Judgment Day˺!
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is invited to imagine seeing the denying polytheists terrified as they behold Allah's punishment, with no possibility of flight or deliverance. The preferred explanation keeps this threat connected to the surrounding account of them, although reports variously locate the terror in worldly punishment or at resurrection.

phrases.translation: And they will be seized from a nearby place
phrases.explanation: They are seized from a nearby place because wherever they are, they remain near to Allah and never beyond His reach. Distance cannot remove them from His punishment. The nearness of the seizure destroys any expectation that a remote refuge or an escape route could keep them safe.

phrases.translation: They will ˹then˺ cry, “We do ˹now˺ believe in it ˹all˺.”
phrases.explanation: When these polytheists see Allah's punishment with their own eyes, they declare faith in Allah, His Book, and His Messenger. The declaration comes only after the reality they denied has become undeniable. At that moment, merely saying that they believe no longer brings the benefit they seek.

phrases.translation: But how could they ˹possibly˺ attain faith from a place so far-off ˹from the world˺
phrases.explanation: They cannot grasp accepted repentance or return from the Hereafter because the opportunity belonged to worldly life, which has passed far beyond reach. Their request to go back comes when return is no longer possible. The related readings convey reaching or delaying, but both express an opportunity now too distant to attain.

phrases.translation: while they had already rejected it before,
phrases.explanation: During worldly life, they had already rejected faith in Allah, Muhammad, and what he brought from his Lord. Their later desire for belief arises only when punishment descends and they want it removed. This contrasts their former deliberate rejection with their sudden profession when escape becomes urgent.

phrases.translation: guessing blindly from a place ˹equally˺ far-away ˹from the Hereafter˺
phrases.explanation: From a position far from knowledge of the unseen, they hurled guesses at Muhammad and Allah's Book. Some called him a sorcerer, soothsayer, or poet, while others denied resurrection, Paradise, and the Fire. These contradictory labels and denials were suppositions and imaginings rather than conclusions based on revealed knowledge.

phrases.translation: They will be sealed off from whatever they desire,
phrases.explanation: A barrier cuts them off from the belief, repentance, or return to worldly life that they now desire after seeing punishment. There is no longer a way to attain what they neglected. Other reports include desires for wealth, children, and worldly splendor, but the immediate context favors their longing for faith.

phrases.translation: as was done to their counterparts before.
phrases.explanation: Earlier disbelieving communities received the same treatment. When Allah's punishment arrived and His power became visible, their sudden belief was not accepted at that moment either. The recurring pattern shows that a profession forced by witnessed retribution does not replace the faith and repentance required beforehand.

phrases.translation: Indeed, they were ˹all˺ in alarming doubt
phrases.explanation: They had lived in disturbing doubt even though their Prophet warned them that persistence in disbelief and idol worship would bring punishment in this world and the Hereafter. Their doubt was neither innocent nor well founded. It kept them from responding to a clear warning until the threatened reality confronted them.
